items.body:
Two field lifecycle fixes. The blur half is a regression from #5460; the filled half predates it.

- **Controlled blur normalization no longer discards validation.** With `validationMode="onBlur"`, a blur handler that normalizes the controlled value (e.g. `.trim()`) had its commit retired by the value's prop transition. The blur handler now re-commits the settled DOM value in a microtask, unless it settled back to the initial value (a programmatic reset stays quiet). Async normalization after blur is still not covered.
- **`filled` is now derived from the current value** in a layout effect (the `NumberField` pattern) instead of transition callbacks and write-only mount effects. This fixes stale `data-filled` on remounts and custom `render` elements in `Field.Control`, `Checkbox.Root`, and `Switch.Root`, and `CheckboxGroup` now fully owns the filled state.

`dirty` stays transition-driven: deriving it needs mount-time `initialValue` ordering guarantees and interacts with #5345.

items.body: A disabled `NavigationMenu.Trigger` didn't expose `data-disabled` (unlike every other trigger), because `disabled` was missing from its state, it was only inherited from `NativeButtonProps`, so it was also undocumented. items.title: [select] Keep controlled value current during item updates

labels.name: component: select
labels.description: Changes related to the select component.

labels.name: scope: store
labels.description: Related to shared store state, subscriptions, or synchronization with React renders.

items.body:
Closes #5875.

## Problem

When a controlled Select changes its `value` and removes the previously selected item in the same React update, `SelectRoot` renders with the new value, but `useSyncedValues` copies it into the store in a layout effect. The item-map callback can run earlier in that commit and read the previous value. It then clears the valid new selection: to `null` in single mode or an empty array in multiple mode.

## Fix

I pass `value`, `multiple`, and `isItemEqualToValue` together through `SelectSelectionContext`. `SelectPositioner` reads those current-render inputs during item reconciliation, before `useSyncedValues` updates the store. Keeping all three inputs together also prevents reconciliation from combining a current value with a stale selection mode or comparator.

`SelectRootContext` remains the store context, preserving its existing name and consumers. The selection context has its own guarded hook and reuses the existing missing-root error message and code. No duplicate error code is added.

I chose a React context so the current-render data flows directly to descendants without relying on the timing of a getter registered through the mutable store context.

The regression tests cover replacing the selected item in single and multiple modes, as well as changing selection mode or comparator alongside the options and value.
